description: Gaia GPS PDF export ('Gaia Topo (feet)', 1 mi scale bar), Langalibalele Pass / Mount Durnford, uKhahlamba-Drakensberg (KwaZulu-Natal / Lesotho). The map is ONE north-up Web Mercator RGB raster (native.png, 1118x791) that the PDF places with '806.4 0 0 561.6 18. 15.68 cm' (99.8 ppi across, 101.4 ppi down), so on the 300 dpi page (map.jpg) one native pixel is 3.0054 px wide and 2.9583 px tall: the page is 1.59 % anisotropic. The white legend band (page y 2310-2415) covers the bottom 35.5 native rows. Truth measured independently of the MapMe core: native px -> Web Mercator is an isotropic, axis-aligned affine, the consensus (mean scale, mean centre) of four estimates: (1) hillshade_terrarium: the map's hillshade (luminance, median-filtered against thin lines, band-passed) against a hillshade of Terrarium z13, NCC maximised over translation, scale and light azimuth/altitude (best light from 320 deg, 66 deg up); (2) hillshade_copernicus: the same against Copernicus GLO-30 (an independent DEM, TanDEM-X based), reprojected to a z14 Mercator grid; (3) contour_layer_terrarium: the brown contour lines alone, by the phase coherence of the Terrarium elevation at the contour pixels modulo the 80 ft interval; (4) via_map_b: map A registered directly onto map B (fixtures/gaia-giants-castle, the same Gaia data at 2.524x the scale; NCC 0.85) composed with B's truth, whose scale is far better determined (B spans 26 km). The four agree with the consensus within 0.87-1.12 native px at the truth points (scale spread 0.19 %); the anisotropic variants of (1)/(2) within 1.41 px. The estimates span 0.19 % in scale (the map's own hillshade fits smallest, the transfer from map B largest) and the two DEMs differ by about 1 native px (~10 m) in absolute position, so the truth is good to about +-1 native px (+-9 m) here. Checks: local translations of 12 windows against each DEM, summit icons against DEM summits, the printed scale bar (implies 9.091 m/px; the truth 9.103, +0.13 %; on map B the bar is 0.19 % off a far better determined fit, so the bars are good to about 0.2 %).
pixel_convention: continuous pixel coordinates: pixel (i, j) covers [i, i+1) x [j, j+1), its centre is (i + 0.5, j + 0.5); x right, y down (as the core: skeleton points sit at pixel centres +0.5)
mercator_convention: X = X0 + sx * x, Y = Y0 - sy * y (Web Mercator metres); pixel_to_mercator is the core's row-major 3x3

raster_placement_pt.note: content stream: "806.4 0 0 561.6 18. 15.68 cm /I0 Do"; top-down the raster spans x 18..824.4 pt, y 18..579.6 pt

checks.window_residuals_note: Each of 12 windows (4 x 3 over the map above the legend band; centres in native px) is registered alone against the DEM hillshade, translation only, holding the truth's scale and light: shift = the local offset in native px (0 where the truth fits exactly).
checks.alternative_fits_note: Each estimate's displacement from the truth (native px) at the 25 truth points: max and rms. m_per_px_scale is Web Mercator metres per native px.
checks.spot_heights_note: Summit icons (template match, centre of the triangle, native px) against the highest Copernicus GLO-30 cell within 210 m: icon_minus_summit_px under the truth, and the DEM summit elevation against the printed spot height (feet). Isolated summits sit within ~1-3 px; icons on the escarpment edge (Erskine, Bond, Potterill, Katana on map A) find a higher cell on the plateau behind them, and Gaia places the same summit's icon differently at different zooms (Mount Durnford: 3 px north of the summit on map A, 7 px on map B), so these check the identification and the scale, not the last pixel.
